steps.text: Heat oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Stir in onion and garlic. Cook and stir until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour, nutritional yeast, and soy sauce to form a smooth paste.
Gradually whisk in broth. Season with sage, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer, stirring constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes, or until thickened. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegetarian Gravy
raw_recipe.description: This easy vegetarian gravy gets a savory boost from nutritional yeast and soy sauce. It makes a great accompaniment to vegan and vegetarian dishes.
raw_recipe.name: Vegetarian Gravy

review.reviewBody: This was a big hit on Thanksgiving. It went perfectly with a Tofurky. I was in a rush and did not read the reviews, so mine came out way too thick. I just added more spices and water until the consistency seemed right to me. Next time I’ll cut back on the oil and flour. The trick to a perfect gravy is to always have equal amounts of fat (oil or butter) and flour so be sure to cut both equally. I also allowed the flour to brown a little before adding the vegetable stock. I think that really adds to the flavor. I would say that the nutritional yeast is not necessary, but it helps a lot. For those who don't know, for some reason nutritional yeast + soy sauce = total goodness. You see that combination in a lot of vegetarian recipes. This will definitely be in my recipe box permanently with some doctoring. I think this recipe would adapt well, like using mushroom broth instead of vegetable. I’ll definitely try it again. Thanks.

I just made this for Thanksgiving and it's so good I've been eating it from the pot and need to put it away or it won't last until then! This is going to be a holiday go-to from now on. After reading the other reviews, I made a few modifications: - Increased the broth to 5 cups, since I wanted more gravy, but left the flour at 1/2 cup (as others have noted, that is way too much flour for the amount of broth, and why I gave the recipe 4 stars instead of 5) - Reduced the oil from 1/2 cup and instead sauteed the onions and garlic in a couple tbsp. each butter and olive oil - Since I used Better Than Bouillon vegetable stock, which is quite salty, it didn't need any additional salt - I didn't have nutritional yeast, so instead used a little San Juan Island Sea Salt popcorn blend, which has nutritional yeast in it - Used a sprig of fresh sage, which I removed after cooking - Strained out the onion and garlic, since I didn't want a chunky gravy. With those changes, this was AMAZING. I think it's far superior to the turkey gravy I made for the meat-eaters.

Needed a vegetarian gravy to bring to a work potluck so all of my coworkers could have some. Decided to try this after reading several reviews.

First, you'll find nutritional yeast in the baking aisle. Took my FOREVER to find it.

Second, as many previous reviews mentioned this will net a VERY thick gravy. Just keep adding more vegetable broth until you get to your consistency.

Last, some people commented about their gravy splitting and becoming oily. This means you didn't emulsify it enough. To avoid this, add the nutritional yeast and flour and cook for a minute, then add the soy sauce to form the paste, then GRADUALLY whisk in the broth. The key word is gradually. Add a quarter cup at a time and whisk until combined, and repeat. I needed to add almost 4 cups before I got to a good gravy consistency.

Fantastic recipe! Will be making this for Thanksgiving this year!

This came out so flavorful I’m shocked. I read the reviews before hand and made some adjustments. I used 1/8 cup oil and 2 tbs of butter to sauté the onions (1/2 cup) and garlic. I toasted the flour and used 1/4 cup to start. I also cut the soy sauce by 2 tbs since I didn’t have low sodium. Towards the end I added a little bit more of flour to thicken it a bit and it was perfect. I am really pleased and grateful for the reviews for the suggestions.

I read a lot of the reviews before making this, and so when I give it 5 stars, it's more that I loved the modified version I came up with. I can guess if I followed it exactly, it would have come out like a gooey paste-like texture. Here are my mods: 2 tbsp Sunflower Oil, 1/3 cup flour, 2 1/2 cups of vegetarian stock, fresh Sage, chopped (kept stems for seasoning the stock), and a pinch of Oregano, Thyme, Marjoram, and Rosemary. I did not add the salt because the stock as well as soy sauce seemed like more than enough salt for me. I first brought the stock to a boil in a separate pan, and put the seasoning and sage stems in, then turned off the heat. I removed the sage stems before using the stock. Once I mixed everything and had a gentle boil and it was thickening, I used a hand blender to make it a smooth gravy (my preference). It turned out great! I have been leaning towards becoming vegan, and this was the closest thing I've had that reminded me of the sage sausage gravy my Mom would make for biscuits. Definitely going to be a staple in our home for holiday dishes.

Great recipe! I didn't read the reviews first and it was indeed a little thick, so I thinned it out with some water and a cube of vegetable bullion so the taste would stay as strong. I added some fresh mushrooms with the onions as well. Yum! Also, I didn't have any sage so I just omitted it and it was still delicious!

Better than traditional gravy! I chopped red onion fairly small, 7 cloves of garlic and used a 1/2 cup butter instead of the oil since my husband and I are vegetarian not vegan. I also just made my own deactivated yeast by toasting a single packet of active dry yeast (2 1/4 tsp) in a small saute pan because I couldn't find it at my local grocery store. I will definitely make this again and again!

Listen, this gravy is absolutely delicious. I rated it only 3 stars as written because there's WAY too much flour. The gravy, as written, is pudding consistency. You have to double everything else to get the right consistency. Or use half the flour/oil to start with.

Going by the other reviews, I halved the fat and the flour. I actually used vegan margarine and potato starch. Cut the garlic by about half and went with mushroom broth--tricky to find, but I think worth it. Subbed white cooking wine for half of the soy sauce. I think Frontier brand nutritional yeast is noticeably better than others I've tried, so I used that. (No financial connection.) I am wild about the taste of standard store-bought poultry seasoning, so I put a scant teaspoon of that in, instead of sage and pepper, and no salt. The result was a minor miracle of flavor for a gravy without turkey drippings. I know it sounds like I barely used the recipe at all, but without the yeast, soy sauce, and fresh sauteed onion from the recipe, I never would have gotten nearly as good results. In fact, I doubt that I would have attempted it. Thank you so much, Becky, for sharing.

This is my go-to vegetarian gravy recipe... Changes that I’d make: use 3 Tbsp of soy sauce, 1/4 cup of flour, and no additional salt or the yeast, otherwise it’s super thick and salty. I also don’t add all of the flour at once. Instead, I sift the flour and add the broth as needed to avoid clumps.

This is a great recipe of ingredients, but the proportions are way off. For starters, the combination of nutritional yeast and soy sauce (I actually prefer Tamari) is the vegetarian equivalent of meaty. So if you aren't going to use these two ingredients - don't bother with this recipe.

Nutritional yeast is an expensive ingredient, so I can see why people will want to omit. Tip - check out Whole Food's bulk bin section.

Here are some adjustments I made:
1) don't add any salt until the end. See if it even needs it at the end.
2) use fresh sage
3) cut the oil in half and add more if necessary
4) add flour slowly until you get the consistency you want, may not require full amount.
5) I added ALOT of nutritional yeast until I got a flavor I liked. Maybe 1/2 - 1 cup.
6) Use some butter instead of oil

Again IMO, this recipe has great ingredients but terrible proportions. That being said, no one touched the meat gravy when I made this.
Best gravy ever. Only one we make at my house. Even the non-vegetarians love it.
This was the most delicious vegetarian gravy ever. I really loved it and will make it on many more occasions.
I took others' advice and reduced the flour. Used shallots (instead of garlic and onions) for a mellower flavor. I would make this again.

This gravy is too thick. Just Add water when you heat it before serving and the problem is solved. Or you can decrease the flour amount. This is the best vegan/vegetarian gravy ever made. I didn't believe some of the reviews that said that meat eaters would like this, but it's totally true! I made this on Thanksgiving and every person that came to the house loved this gravy, including the meat eaters. This recipe is a keeper for sure. My sister said, "I need the recipe for that if you don’t mind sharing. It was truly the best gravy. It was so sage-y and yummy all around."
Delicious! Minor complaint: comes out a bit too thick in my experience, and on day 2 it's more of a gel than a liquid... Might try adding more broth next time.
This is great as written but those who mention mushrooms are on to something and I can’t wait to try!
Excellent base and measurements however, I use butter instead of oil… And always use fresh rosemary, sage, and thyme while I'm cooking it… For that beautiful savory flavor
This went very well with Veggie Steaks (AKA MorningStar Steakhouse burgers) with carmelized onions and mushrooms. Quick and easy recipe with items I already had on hand.
